title: Ursinus/Paraeus: reigning vs non-reigning sin
source_text: XXII. Eodem vero recidit distinctio peccati in regnans & non regnans; prout illam tradit & explicat Ursinus in Catecheticis explicationibus Davidis Paraei opera recognitis. Peccatum regnans, inquit, est cui peccans non repugnat per gratiam Spiritus Sancti, ideoque fit obnoxius aeternae morti, nisi poenitentiam agat, & veniam per Christum consequatur. Seu est omne peccatum quod non deploratur, & cui non resistitur per gratiam Spiritus Sancti, & propter quod, non tantum ex ordine justitiae Dei, sed ex reipsa, aeternarum poenarum reus est qui illud habet. Talia sunt omnia peccata in non renatis: quaedam etiam in renatis, ut error in fundamento fidei, & lapsus contra conscientiam, cum quibus fiducia remissionis peccatorum, & consolatio vera non consistit, donec resipiscant. Quod enim etiam renati possint cadere in peccatum regnans, satis ostendunt tristissimi lapsus sanctissimorum hominum, ut Aaronis, Davidis, &c. Non regnans peccatum est cui peccans repugnat per gratiam Spiritus Sancti: ideoque non est obnoxius aeternae morti, quia poenitentiam agit, & veniam consequitur per Christum. Talia peccata sunt omnes defectus, inclinationes, & cupiditates pravae, & multa peccata ignorantiae, omissionis & infirmitatis, reliquiae in sanctis, quamdiu sunt in hac vita, quae tamen agnoscunt, deplorant, & oderunt, & in quibus etiam fidem & consolationem retinent. Parte prima, titulo De peccato Actuali.
pass_a_gloss: But to the same comes the distinction of sin into reigning and not reigning; as Ursinus hands it down and explains it in the Catechetical Explications revised by the labor of David Paraeus. Reigning sin, he says, is that which the sinner does not resist by the grace of the Holy Spirit, and therefore he becomes liable to eternal death unless he repents and obtains pardon through Christ. Or it is every sin that is not bewailed, and that is not resisted by the grace of the Holy Spirit, and on account of which he who has it is guilty of eternal penalties not only by the order of God’s justice but in very deed. Such are all sins in the unregenerate: some also in the regenerate, as error in the foundation of faith, and falls against conscience, with which confidence of the remission of sins and true consolation do not stand until they repent. For that even the regenerate can fall into reigning sin the most sad falls of the most holy men, as of Aaron, David, etc., sufficiently show. Non-reigning sin is that which the sinner resists by the grace of the Holy Spirit: and therefore he is not liable to eternal death, because he repents and obtains pardon through Christ. Such sins are all defects, inclinations, and wicked desires, and many sins of ignorance, omission, and infirmity, remains in the saints so long as they are in this life, which nevertheless they acknowledge, bewail, and hate, and in which they also retain faith and consolation. Part one, title On actual sin.
pass_b_english: Ursinus (via Paraeus): reigning sin is unresisted and actually death-liable—found in all the unregenerate and in some regenerate falls.
Non-reigning sin is Spirit-resisted; saints keep faith and comfort amid remaining infirmities they hate.
